messages:
alice-cs: Hey team, multiple customers are seeing SSE streams cut off after ~30s. They report partial output then the connection closes. Happening across ALB + Cloudflare in front of our hosted API. No clear error in client (just EOF).

maria-support: Thanks Alice — can you paste one of the request examples and any correlation id? Is this consistently reproducible for the same model/route?

alice-cs: Repro for me: curl to our /v1/stream endpoint with ephemeral JWT that refreshes via refresh_token flow. curl: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $EPHEMERAL" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-xyz
```
Customer logs show connection at 12:02:31, last event chunk at 12:02:58, then TCP FIN. No 4xx/5xx from upstream. Correlation id x-cid=cid-9f2a

ingest-bot: [automated] Ingested logs for cid-9f2a: upstream returned 200 then connection reset by peer at 27s. No request-level 401 recorded.

maria-support: Hmm. Any CDN or proxy in front? You mentioned Cloudflare + ALB?

alice-cs: Yes: Cloudflare in front of an ALB which forwards to nginx/uwsgi stack. We recently enabled gzip and left default idle timeouts on ALB.

devon-engineer: This smells like a keepalive/flush + compression + token rotation interplay. SSE needs chunked responses that flush. If gzip is enabled and the proxy buffers until a window fills or until the upstream signals EOF, Cloudflare/ALB might not flush partial chunks to the client. If the token rotation hits and a refresh causes a follow-up request or an ALB healthcheck to interrupt, connection can get reset.

ops-jay: Also check ALB idle timeout vs Cloudflare's origin keepalive. If ALB times out connections (default 60s) but CF expects a different behavior, you can see mid-stream resets. But your symptom at ~27s is interesting — could be client-side abort when it sees a silence (no chunk boundary) if keepalives suppressed.

maria-support: Can you capture a tcpdump or curl --trace? Also try bypassing Cloudflare (direct to ALB) to see if it repros.

alice-cs: Quick repro we did: direct-to-ALB still repros but only when gzip enabled on nginx. When we disabled gzip for the /v1/stream route, streams stay open. So compression seems correlated.

devon-engineer: Yep. Gzip + nginx proxy_buffering can buffer small writes. For SSE we want immediate flushing. Suggested nginx config changes for SSE path:

```
location /v1/stream {
  # disable gzip for event-stream
  gzip off;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache off;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  # increase timeouts so ALB/CF don't prematurely close
  proxy_read_timeout 300s;
  proxy_send_timeout 300s;
}
```
Also ensure the app sets `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and calls flush after each event.

maria-support: Another angle: ephemeral token rotation mid-stream may cause the app to try a background refresh or cause a client to re-auth; did the customers show any refresh activity exactly at disconnect time?

alice-cs: They do rotate tokens ~30s after issuance. But the flow is client-side; the server shouldn't care. However, if a second request (like a token refresh or healthcheck) opens a new connection and the ALB reuses or closes backend sockets, that can knock the original stream.

devon-engineer: Right — ALB uses keepalive between ALB and backend. If backend (nginx) has connection pooling and a healthcheck or a new request triggers a premature backend socket close, the active upstream streaming socket can get reset. Make sure your nginx `keepalive_timeout` and ALB `idle_timeout` are aligned. Also avoid reusing backend sockets for long-lived streamed responses. One mitigation: set `proxy_set_header Connection "";` and `proxy_http_version 1.1;` with `proxy_set_header Connection keep-alive;` tuned so ALB doesn't try to multiplex incorrectly.

ops-jay: For Cloudflare specifically, disable HTTP/2 to origin for SSE paths or ensure Cloudflare's "Origin Keep-alive Timeout" is long enough. Cloudflare can terminate SSE or buffer depending on config (and some CF plans force buffering/gzip).

alice-cs: We tested disabling gzip + proxy_buffering off and increasing proxy_read_timeout → resolved for the customer. They said streams now stay up for the expected durations.

maria-support: Great. Can we capture the exact mitigation steps to close the ticket and add a KB? Also include a fallback SDK change: detect 5s of silence and emit a client-side reconnect with last-event-id so users don't miss output.

devon-engineer: Draft KB snippet: Steps to mitigate SSE truncation with CF/ALB/nginx: 
1) Disable gzip for SSE endpoints (nginx `gzip off` for that location).
2) Turn off proxy buffering (`proxy_buffering off`) so nginx flushes chunks immediately.
3) Ensure `chunked_transfer_encoding on` and `Content-Type: text/event-stream` with explicit flush in app.
4) Align ALB idle timeout >= expected stream duration and set `proxy_read_timeout` > ALB timeout.
5) If using Cloudflare, enable "pass-through" or disable origin response modification for SSE paths; consider bypassing CF for long-lived streams.
6) Avoid server-side token refresh flows that reuse/close backend sockets mid-stream. Prefer stateless validation of ephemeral tokens or extend rotation window for streaming.

maria-support: Also add a small troubleshooting command: curl that reproduces the behavior so customers can test themselves:
```
# reproduce - stream with no buffering
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EPHEMERAL" \
  --http1.1 \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream > /dev/null
```

alice-cs: I've updated the customer with the nginx snippet and asked them to confirm. They replied: 

customer (external): confirmed — disabled gzip for that route and set proxy_buffering off; stream runs for full 10m session now. Thanks! :tada:

maria-support: Nice. Closing CTA: create KB and recommend SDK patch to auto-reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` handling.

deploy-bot: [deploy] KB draft pushed to docs repo at refs/changes/streaming-proxy-sse-kb ; CI passed.

maria-support: Assigning follow-up to devon-engineer to draft SDK reconnect snippet and to ops-jay to add recommended ALB/Cloudflare config to runbook.

devon-engineer: Will do. Quick SDK snippet suggestion for clients to resume SSE: on disconnect, do a GET with `Last-Event-ID` header and server should stream from last checkpoint (if server supports resumable chunks). Otherwise fallback to restart and include server-side idempotency markers.

alice-cs: Thanks everyone. Ticket closed by customer. :white_check_mark:
